 8th Pay Commission: Will 4x Fitment Factor Bring ₹15.20 Lakh Arrears for Govt Employees? 
 8th Pay Commission: Will 4x Fitment Factor Bring ₹15.20 Lakh Arrears for Govt Employees?
 Discussions about the 8th Pay Commission are heating up. Employees are curious about the expected salary hike and arrears.
 7 Min read Author : Richa Barua Published : Nov 13 2026, 11:44 AM IST Share this Photo Gallery FB 
 TW 
 Linkdin 
 Whatsapp 
 GN Follow Us 
 1 10 Image Credit : Asianet News How much will the salary hike be?
 The buzz around the 8th Pay Commission is growing among central government employees and pensioners. Everyone is asking: how much will the salary increase? What will be the new minimum basic pay? Will we get arrears running into lakhs? A popular calculation floating around suggests a 4.00 Fitment Factor. If applied, current basic salaries could quadruple. For instance, an employee drawing a basic pay of Rs 53,100 right now could see it jump to Rs 2,12,400. This calculation also estimates 12-month arrears of up to Rs 15.20 lakh. However, this is just a calculation, not a guaranteed payout. The 4.00 Fitment Factor is an assumption. Let us break down how these calculations and arrears actually work. Add Asianet Newsable as a Preferred Source 2 10 Image Credit : Asianet News When will the 8th Pay Commission roll out?
 The 7th Pay Commission cycle officially wraps up on December 31, 2025. This has naturally spiked expectations for the 8th Pay Commission. The government formed the 8th Pay Commission on November 3, 2025, appointing Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai as the chairperson. Professor Pulak Ghosh serves as a part-time member, and Pankaj is the member secretary. The panel has 18 months to submit its recommendations. We can expect the final report by May 2027. But remember, the report submission date is not the implementation date. The central government will review the recommendations and get cabinet approval before rolling out the new pay scales. A big question is whether the benefits will be calculated from January 1, 2026. If they are, employees will likely receive arrears for the gap period even if the actual rollout is delayed.  8th Pay Commission Update: Will You Get Pension Arrears if You Retire Before Implementation? 8th Pay Commission: AIRF Presents 6 Demands To 8th Pay Commission For Railway Employees 3 10 Image Credit : Asianet News What is the 4 Fitment Factor? Why does it matter?
 The Fitment Factor is the hottest topic in the 8th Pay Commission discussions. It is the formula used to convert the old basic salary into the new one. Simply put, you multiply your current basic pay by this specific number to get your new basic pay. For example, a 2.00 factor means double the basic pay. The 7th Pay Commission used a 2.57 Fitment Factor. The big debate now is what factor the 8th Pay Commission will lock in. Various employee unions are demanding different fitment factors to maximize their salary hikes. 4 10 Image Credit : Asianet News How much will salaries jump with a 4x Fitment Factor?
 If the government agrees to a 4.00 Fitment Factor, salaries will see a massive change. The math is simple: New Basic Salary = Current Basic Salary × 4. This means your basic pay becomes four times larger, effectively a 300 percent increase. Let us take a Level 9 employee currently earning a basic pay of Rs 53,100. With a 4.00 Fitment Factor, the new estimated basic pay hits Rs 2,12,400. That is a difference of Rs 1,59,300 in the monthly basic salary alone. Keep in mind, this is purely an assumption based on the 4.00 factor. The actual salary fixing will depend on the new Pay Matrix, pay levels, DA, and other rules. 5 10 Image Credit : Asianet News How does a Rs 53,100 salary result in Rs 15.20 lakh arrears?
 The 12-month arrear calculation is catching everyone's eye. Let us assume the 8th Pay Commission benefits start from January 1, 2026, but the actual payout happens in late 2027. Employees would get arrears for that gap. To understand this, let us stick with our Level 9 employee earning a basic salary of Rs 53,100. If we use the 4 factor, their new basic pay becomes Rs 2,12,400. This calculation also assumes the Dearness Allowance (DA) will be 60 percent from January to June 2026, and 63 percent from July to December. These DA rates are just estimates. The crucial point is how the old DA merges with the new basic pay. Will the DA reset to zero on the new pay scale, or will the old DA continue? The Rs 15.20 lakh arrear figure assumes DA starts at zero on the new basic pay, while you still get the DA owed on the old structure. Again, this is an expectation-based calculation, not an official government promise. 6 10 Image Credit : Asianet News Breaking down the arrears: Jan to June 2026
 Let us calculate the arrears for the first half of 2026. Taking the old basic pay of Rs 53,100 and assuming a 60 percent DA (Rs 31,860), the total monthly pay is Rs 84,960. On the flip side, the new assumed basic pay is Rs 2,12,400. The monthly difference between the new basic pay and the old total pay is Rs 1,27,440. Multiply that by six months, and you get arrears of Rs 7,64,640 for Jan-June 2026. For July-Dec 2026, let us assume DA hits 63 percent. The old basic pay plus DA (Rs 33,453) equals Rs 86,553 per month. The monthly difference from the new basic pay (Rs 2,12,400) is Rs 1,25,847. Over six months, that is Rs 7,55,082. Adding both periods together, the total 12-month arrears touch Rs 15,19,722, or roughly Rs 15.20 lakh. Remember, this applies to a Level 9 employee assuming a 4.00 Fitment Factor. The actual arrears will completely depend on the final government orders regarding the implementation date, fitment factor, and DA merger. 7 10 Image Credit : Asianet News What arrears could other Pay Level employees get?
 If a 4.00 Fitment Factor becomes reality, expectations are soaring for arrears across different Pay Levels. Using the same 12-month calculation (Jan-Dec 2026) with estimated DA rates, the numbers are huge. For Level 1 employees, an old basic of Rs 18,000 jumps to Rs 72,000, potentially yielding Rs 5.15 lakh in arrears. Level 2 might see Rs 5.69 lakh, and Level 3 around Rs 6.21 lakh. As you go up the ladder, the estimates climb. Level 4 could get Rs 7.29 lakh, Level 6 around Rs 10.13 lakh, and Level 8 about Rs 13.62 lakh. We already saw Level 9 hitting Rs 15.19 lakh. Level 11 could see Rs 19.37 lakh, and Level 12 might reach Rs 22.55 lakh. At the top end, Level 14 could fetch Rs 41.27 lakh, and the highest Level 18 might even touch Rs 71.55 lakh. However, these are strictly hypothetical calculations based on assumed DA rates and a 4.00 Fitment Factor. None of this is official yet. We have to wait for the final government directives to know the actual arrears. 8 10 Image Credit : Asianet News Will pensioners also benefit?
 The 8th Pay Commission will heavily impact pensioners as well, not just serving employees. Recommendations regarding basic pension, family pension, and other retirement benefits are eagerly awaited. Pensioners are keeping a close watch on how the Fitment Factor will revise their basic pension. For instance, a basic pension of Rs 25,000 could hit Rs 1 lakh under a 4.00 Fitment Factor. But again, this is purely mathematical speculation. The final rules for pension revision are pending. Pensioners will have to wait for official government notifications to confirm their revised payouts and arrears. 9 10 Image Credit : Asianet News Will the new salary rollout happen by late 2027?
 The 8th Pay Commission should submit its report by May 2027. After that, the government will review it and make a decision. Looking at past pay commissions, the new salaries never start immediately after the report drops. The 5th Pay Commission submitted its report in Jan 1997 but got approval in Oct 1997. The 6th Pay Commission submitted in March 2008 and got the green light in Aug 2008. The 7th Pay Commission report came in Nov 2015 and saw approval in June 2016. Going by this trend, it will take months after the 8th Pay Commission report submission before things finalize. Many predict the rollout might happen in late 2027 or early 2028. But there is no confirmed timeline yet. 10 10 Image Credit : gemini Crucial update for government employees!
 The 8th Pay Commission will definitely bring changes to salaries and pensions. But do not treat the viral WhatsApp forwards about a 4.00 Fitment Factor, a Rs 2,12,400 new basic salary, or Rs 15.20 lakh arrears as the final truth. The commission officially has 18 months to submit its recommendations. While January 1, 2026, is the expected effective date based on the 10-year cycle, it is not the final implementation order yet. Employees can hope for a high Fitment Factor, but they must rely on official announcements. The final Fitment Factor, pay scales, and arrear rules announced by the government will ultimately decide the real benefits.
